content:
GOAL: Compare CURVCELL-SID (A) vs SUCCFAN-CURV-RQ (B) on rubric-2026-10-v1 over the frozen bundles e9e97242e0e9ed08, 404ea254563870a6, bc19762831440f87. No filesystem write access; analysis done from the printed bundle only.
READ: Both idea specs; behavioural evidence E1-E11 (identical shared block across bundles); geometry E12-E14 for each; cost/risk sections.
OBSERVED: (1) Shared measured evidence is the same for both: E5 successor-entropy stratification (top1 mass 0.4375 low-entropy vs 0.0543 high, Spearman(entropy,top1)=-0.9733, bin5 support 44.3), E8 first-level capacity ceiling (pair-share K=16 0.3106 vs K=256 0.0822), E6 beam survival where every successor-curvature SID variant lost to the Euclidean/plain controls (l1_br 0.04671, successor_entropy 0.05122, successor_geodesic_coarse 0.05500 vs l1_br_euclid 0.06207, l1_only 0.06233, resample 0.06363).
(2) A is fully specified: closed-form s=log(1+B)/((d-1)R), 12 fixed refresh epochs, cumulative-mean update (no tuned decay), clamp, no gradient into s, per-pair extra multiply 1023*256*4=1.05M FLOPs, three matched switches (behaviour-off => s=1 = unit-curvature baseline; geometry-off keeps weights, drops curvature).
(3) B's spec is a pointer ("See SPEC EQUATIONS"), not an implementation; B's geometry-off control is internally inconsistent: lambda=2/(1-c||x||^2) at c->0 is 2, not 1, so the geometry-off arm carries an extra global factor 2 and differs from the intended switch.
(4) B's cost section says 3x256 scalar lambdas per level, but its mechanism is per-prefix-node curvature, i.e. K^l nodes; per-node curvature at levels 2-3 cannot be stored in 3x256 scalars. B's E14 slot is empty.
(5) E6 shows the same family (successor geometry folded into SID construction/curvature) already produced a measured negative at this scale, which bears on exploration_value for B and on novelty distance for A.
REASONING: A wins on implementability (fully specified, guarded, budgeted), on falsifiability (matched switches + explicit falsifier Spearman(|A_k|,B_k)~0 => encoder absorbs behaviour), and on exploration_value (self-consistent EM field is not the measured negative family; B is close to successor_geodesic_coarse which already lost). A is weaker on geometry_necessity because d_B/s is a per-code scalar divisor that a weighted Euclidean distance may reproduce.
OPEN: Whether A's geometry_necessity should be scored 2 or 3 given the per-code scale divisor, and whether the E6 negative transfers from the probe generator to Stage 2.

ANSWER RECORD.
WINNER: CURVCELL-SID
FIRST LISTED: CURVCELL-SID
ARGUMENT: (i) implementability + falsifiability (10%/10%): A's spec is executable to the scalar (closed-form s, 12 fixed refresh epochs, cumulative mean, clamp, no gradient into s, 1.05M extra FLOPs) and its two switches are matched, whereas B is a pointer to unpasted equations, bills 3x256 lambdas per level for a mechanism defined per prefix node (K^l nodes), leaves E14 empty, and its geometry-off control is mis-specified because lambda(c->0)=2 not 1, so the control differs from the intended switch. (ii) exploration_value/novelty (5%/20%): E6 already records the measured negative in B's family - successor_entropy 0.05122 and successor_geodesic_coarse 0.05500 recall@10 against l1_br_euclid 0.06207 / l1_only 0.06233 / resample 0.06363 - and B is a per-node re-run of that same curvature-on-successor recipe, while A adds a self-consistent EM loop (behaviour calibrates curvature -> curvature reshapes cells) that has not been measured here. (iii) downstream_mechanism/behaviour_evidence (15%/20%): A names the affected assignment (argmin and commitment at every residual level), the observable and direction (H(next code | level-0 code) falls, Spearman(|A_k|,B_k) positive) and anchors it in E5's measured branching spread (top1 0.4375 vs 0.0543, bin5 support 44.3) plus E8's measured capacity ceiling (0.3106 at K=16 vs 0.0822 at K=256), so its chain from cell size to prefix survival is auditable; B asserts higher code entropy in the top fanout quartile is good, which E6 does not support.
FAILURE RISK: A's curvature enters only as a per-code scalar divisor d_B(eps,c)/s, so the encoder can cancel it (s takes no gradient and the argmin only moves if boundaries actually move), and the self-consistent loop can drift to a few huge low-curvature cells or oscillate at refresh epochs; if a matched per-code weighted-Euclidean control reproduces A's partition and recall, the geometry is unnecessary and the choice is wrong on 20% geometry_necessity, with the Spearman(|A_k|,B_k) diagnostic positive but H and Recall@10 flat.
That is the complete answer.
